title: Narrative
description: A narrative is composed of one Story (the fabula: what happened) and one or more Discourses (the syuzhet: how it is told). Events, locations, times, and participants are defined once at the top level and referenced by id from anywhere in the document.

events.description: All events that occur in the story. Referenced by id from Story.eventIds, Fragment.eventIds, and Event.causedByEventIds.

Identifier.description: A stable, unique identifier within this document.

PresenceType.description: How a participant is present in an event. ACTIVE: drives the action. PASSIVE: present and affected but not driving. MENTIONED: referenced in narration or dialogue without being physically present.

Sentiment.description: The overall affective valence of a directed interaction (effectively the from-participant's affect toward the to-participant, since interactions are directional).

Role.description: The narrative role a participant plays in an event (e.g. protagonist, antagonist, helper, victim, witness, mentor, foil). Kept as an open string so authors can use vocabularies suited to their corpus, but a recommended inventory is offered for validation and tooling consistency. Recommended values: PROTAGONIST, ANTAGONIST, HELPER, VICTIM, WITNESS, MENTOR, FOIL, DONOR, PROP (for object-domain participants with narrative significance).

Story.description: The fabula: the ordered set of events that constitute what happened, independent of how it is told.

eventIds.description: References to events in the top-level events array. A story has at least one event (1..*).

Discourse.description: A particular telling of the story: a sequence of fragments in some medium.

Fragment.description: A unit of discourse (a paragraph, shot, panel, audio clip...) that references exactly one event from the story. An event may be referenced by many fragments.

fragment.description: The medium of this individual fragment. Defaults to the discourse medium but can differ for mixed-medium discourses.

eventId.description: The Event this fragment references (references association in the UML, multiplicity Event 1 — * Fragment).

Event.description: A single occurrence in the story. Events are ordered within the story by their position in Story.eventIds.

causedByEventIds.description: Events that cause this event (causes self-association, modeled here as inbound references).

partOfEventIds.description: Larger events that this event is part of (partOf self-association — mereology, distinct from causality).

participations.description: Participants involved in this event and the role they play. Each Participation carries a unique entryOrder within this event (UML qualifier on the belongsTo association).

interactions.description: Directed interactions between participants that occur within this event. Each Interaction carries a unique temporalOrder within this event (UML qualifier on the has association).

Participation.description: A participant's involvement in an event. Acts as the association class between Event and Participant. entryOrder is the UML qualifier on the belongsTo association: it indexes participations within their parent Event, so that 'the participant who appears first in this event' is well-defined. Within a single Event, no two Participations share an entryOrder.

entryOrder.description: Order in which this participant enters the event. Unique within its parent Event.

presenceType.description: Optional: how this participant is present in the event (active, passive, or mentioned).

Interaction.description: A directed action from one participant to another within an event. temporalOrder is the UML qualifier on the has association: it indexes interactions within their parent Event, so that 'the interaction that happens first during this event' is well-defined. Within a single Event, no two Interactions share a temporalOrder.

temporalOrder.description: Order in which this interaction occurs during the event. Unique within its parent Event.

sentiment.description: Optional: overall affective valence of this directed interaction.

value.description: Lexical value; interpretation depends on type (ISO date, time, duration, or set/recurrence).

Participant.description: An entity that can participate in events or interactions: an individual, a set/group, or an object.
